UNHCR reported an EU High Representative visit to a partner-supported legal clinic in Damascus, including meetings with displaced people and returnees.
UN-Habitat and partners announced completion of work to restore water access and repair associated urban infrastructure in eastern Aleppo.
Japan and UN-Habitat announced a programme for public-space renewal and municipal waste management in Homs.
UNHCR’s April–June monitoring recorded conflict-related safety concerns in As-Sweida and access constraints across the southern region.
Community consultations described psychosocial distress, social-cohesion concerns and difficult living conditions in the coastal region.
UNHCR reported opening a community centre in Al-Shaddadi to support protection and returnee reintegration.
UNHCR reported partner training in community engagement, feedback and complaints mechanisms in Qamishli and Ar-Raqqa.
UNHCR reported assisting returns from six displacement sites in Deir-ez-Zor as part of a programme spanning several governorates.
UNHCR’s north-west findings connect return movements with pressure on housing, livelihoods, documentation and essential services.
UNHCR reported that rehabilitation of civil-registry centres in Nawa and Haran Al-Awamid had commenced, with improved access to documentation as the stated aim.
UNHCR reported legal counselling and awareness work particularly in Al-Hasakeh and Ar-Raqqa in connection with a nationality-documentation programme.
UNHCR reported training in Qamishli and Ar-Raqqa on engagement with affected communities and feedback and complaints mechanisms.
The protection factsheet lists a Douma initiative to create a centre for children with autism and Down syndrome among selected community-organization projects.
UNHCR reported that it and Première Urgence Internationale had started rehabilitation of the Al-Bab Vocational Training Centre after preparatory assessments.
